description: Pull request flow: review, approval, the merge queue, rebases and E2E reruns.

panels.title: Merged
panels.description: Pull requests merged. Population: pull requests merged in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: count.

panels.title: Open to merge
panels.description: Median time from opening to merge. Population: pull requests merged in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: duration.

panels.title: Open to merge, slow
panels.description: The 90th percentile: 9 in 10 merged pull requests took less. Population: pull requests merged in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: duration.

panels.title: Wait for first review
panels.description: Median time from ready for review (or opening) to the first human review. Population: pull requests merged in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: duration.

panels.title: Review to approval
panels.description: Median time from the first human review to the first approval. Population: pull requests merged in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: duration.

panels.title: First approval to queue
panels.description: Median time from the first approval to entering the merge queue. A pull request that needs two working groups waits here for the second one; Last approval to queue, below, starts at the last approval. Population: pull requests merged in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: duration.

panels.title: In the merge queue
panels.description: Median time from entering the merge queue to the end of its last attempt. Population: pull requests merged in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: duration.

panels.title: Ejected from the queue
panels.description: Share of the queued pull requests whose own merge-queue checks failed or timed out at least once. A cancelled entry is not an ejection: every entry behind a failing one is cancelled and queued again. Population: pull requests merged in the selected repository that entered the merge queue. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: percent.

panels.title: Commits per PR
panels.description: Median commits of a merged pull request. Population: pull requests merged in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: commits.

panels.title: Rebased
panels.description: Share of the merged pull requests force-pushed at least once (a rebase or a rewrite). Population: pull requests merged in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: percent.

panels.title: Force pushes per PR
panels.description: Average force pushes of a merged pull request. Population: pull requests merged in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: force pushes per pull request.

panels.title: Changes requested
panels.description: Share of the merged pull requests that got a 'changes requested' review. Population: pull requests merged in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: percent.

panels.title: E2E runs per PR
panels.description: Median E2E suite runs of a pull request that ran E2E. Population: merged pull requests in the selected repository with at least one VMaaS, CaaS or BMaaS E2E run (pull-request and merge-queue runs); most pull requests change nothing a suite tests. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: runs per pull request.

panels.title: Extra E2E runs per PR
panels.description: Median E2E runs beyond the first of each suite (a re-run or a new run of the same suite) of a pull request that ran E2E. Population: merged pull requests in the selected repository with at least one VMaaS, CaaS or BMaaS E2E run (pull-request and merge-queue runs); most pull requests change nothing a suite tests. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: runs per pull request.

panels.title: PRs with a failed E2E
panels.description: Share of the pull requests that ran E2E with at least one failed E2E run. Population: merged pull requests in the selected repository with at least one VMaaS, CaaS or BMaaS E2E run (pull-request and merge-queue runs); most pull requests change nothing a suite tests. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: percent.

panels.title: Ejected · re-queued
panels.description: Merge-queue attempts that did not merge. Ejected: the attempt's own checks failed or timed out. Re-queued: the attempt was cancelled or replaced by a later one, which happens to every entry behind a failing one, after a new push, or when the pull request is taken out by hand. Population: attempts of pull requests merged in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: count of attempts.

panels.title: Review rounds
panels.description: Median number of versions of the code that got a human review, per pull request. A review records the commit it looked at, so a rebase does not hide a round. Population: merged pull requests read with the lifecycle (Lifecycle measured), in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: count.

panels.title: Re-approved after a push
panels.description: Share of the pull requests that had to be approved again after the code changed: an approval by a reviewer, or for a team, that had approved an earlier version. Population: merged pull requests read with the lifecycle (Lifecycle measured), in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: percent.

panels.title: Re-review after a rebase
panels.description: Share of the pull requests approved again after a force push (a rebase or a rewrite) came between the two approvals. Population: merged pull requests read with the lifecycle (Lifecycle measured), in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: percent.

panels.title: Wait for a re-approval
panels.description: Median time from the last push to the approval of it, over the pull requests that were re-approved (their longest such wait). Population: merged pull requests read with the lifecycle (Lifecycle measured), in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: duration.

panels.title: Last approval to queue
panels.description: Median time from the last approval before the merge queue to entering it. The first approval to queue tile above starts at the first approval, which for a pull request that needs two working groups is the first of them. Population: merged pull requests read with the lifecycle (Lifecycle measured), in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: duration.

panels.title: Files per PR
panels.description: Median number of files a pull request changed, as GitHub counts them. Population: merged pull requests with their size and code-owner teams read, in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: count.

panels.title: Needed 2+ WGs
panels.description: Share of the pull requests that needed two or more working groups (code-owner teams) to approve. Population: merged pull requests with their size and code-owner teams read, in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: percent.

panels.title: Lifecycle measured
panels.description: Merged pull requests whose lifecycle is read (event list, review rounds, working groups), out of all merged. A row stored before the lifecycle existed is read again by the backfill. Population: merged pull requests in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: count.

panels.title: Stage medians per week
panels.description: The median of each stage per week of the merge. A rising line is a stage pull requests wait longer in. Population: pull requests merged in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: one point per week of the merge (the Monday), last $days days. Unit: duration.

panels.title: Every merged pull request: time to merge
panels.description: One dot per merged pull request: when it merged, across, and how long it took from opening to merge, up, on a log scale (each line is ten times the one below). The color is how many working groups had to approve it. Hover a dot for the pull request; click it to open it below. Population: merged pull requests in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: hours.

properties.value: hours from opening to merge (log scale)

panels.title: Time to merge, week by week
panels.description: Each column is a week of merges, each cell the pull requests merged that week whose time from opening to merge falls in that band, the fastest at the bottom; the darker, the more. A column whose cells climb is a week of slower merges. Population: merged pull requests in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: one column per week of the merge (the Monday), last $days days. Unit: count of pull requests.

panels.title: Where the time goes, by working groups to approve
panels.description: The average time a merged pull request spent in each state, by how many working groups had to approve it. A bar is the average time from opening to merge and its parts add up to it. Waiting for another WG runs from the first working group's approval to the last one's. The label counts the pull requests. Population: merged pull requests read with the lifecycle, in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: duration.

defaults.noValue: No pull request read with the lifecycle in this window.

panels.title: Where the time goes, by files changed
panels.description: The average time a merged pull request spent in each state, by how many files it changed. A bar is the average time from opening to merge and its parts add up to it. Waiting for another WG runs from the first working group's approval to the last one's. The label counts the pull requests. Population: merged pull requests read with the lifecycle, in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: duration.

defaults.noValue: No pull request read with the lifecycle in this window.

panels.title: Review rounds per pull request
panels.description: How many versions of the code got a human review before the merge. Population: merged pull requests read with the lifecycle, in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: count of pull requests.

defaults.noValue: No pull request read with the lifecycle in this window.

panels.title: Times in the merge queue
panels.description: How many times a pull request entered the merge queue before it merged; more than once is a removal (failed checks, a conflict, taken out by hand) and a new try. Population: merged pull requests read with the lifecycle, in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: count of pull requests.

defaults.noValue: No pull request read with the lifecycle in this window.

panels.title: Working groups that had to approve
panels.description: How many working groups (code-owner teams) had to approve a pull request, as GitHub reports them. Population: merged pull requests read with the lifecycle, in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: count of pull requests.

defaults.noValue: No pull request read with the lifecycle in this window.

panels.title: The slowest pull requests, stretch by stretch
panels.description: The 20 merged pull requests that took longest from opening to merge, each bar its whole way, every stretch colored by where the pull request was. Read a bar left to right; a color that comes back is the pull request going around again: another review round, a re-review after a push, another try in the merge queue. After eight rounds the rest is added to the eighth. Click a bar to open the pull request below. Population: the 20 slowest merged pull requests read with the lifecycle, in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: duration.

defaults.noValue: No pull request read with the lifecycle in this window.

panels.title: Pull requests
panels.description: Every pull request merged or closed, the newest first; click a column header to sort, Total for the longest. Click the number to open it below; the title opens it on GitHub. Files: files changed. WGs: working groups that had to approve, and which. Rounds: versions of the code that got a review. Re-approved: approvals given again after the code changed. Authoring: opened to first review. Review: first review to approval. Waiting: approval to the merge queue. Queue: in the merge queue. Ejected: queue attempts whose own checks failed. Re-queued: queue attempts cancelled or replaced, not failed. Population: pull requests merged or closed in the selected repository, author and working groups. Time: merged or closed in the last $days days (the Window above). Unit: duration and count.

panels.title: Total
panels.description: Opened to merged or closed. Not measured when a boundary is missing.

panels.title: Authoring
panels.description: Opened to the first human review.

panels.title: Review
panels.description: First human review to the first human approval.

panels.title: Waiting
panels.description: First human approval to the first merge-queue attempt.

panels.title: Queue
panels.description: First merge-queue attempt to the last.

panels.title: Lifecycle
panels.description: Where the pull request was at every moment from opening to merge, stretch by stretch, numbered in order: a draft, waiting for a reviewer, with the author after review comments, waiting for another working group, approved but not queued, in the merge queue, out of the queue after a removal. The legend lists the stretches with their durations; What happened, below, lists the events that moved it. Population: the selected pull request. Time: opened to merged or closed; an open pull request to now. Unit: duration.

defaults.noValue: Not measured yet: the backfill reads this pull request again.

panels.title: What happened
panels.description: Every event of the pull request, oldest first: opened, ready, review requests, reviews and who they counted for, pushes, force pushes (rebases), the base branch merged in, dismissed approvals, merge when ready, entries into and removals from the merge queue with GitHub's reason, the merge. Click an event to open it on GitHub. Population: the selected pull request. Time: opened to merged or closed. Unit: time after opening, d hh:mm:ss.

defaults.noValue: Not measured yet: the backfill reads this pull request again.

panels.title: This pull request in numbers
panels.description: Its size, the working groups that had to approve it, its review rounds and re-approvals, its pushes and its times in the merge queue. Population: the selected pull request. Time: opened to merged or closed. Unit: as each line says.

panels.title: Queue attempts
panels.description: Each merge-queue entry, how long it lasted, and how it ended. Ejected: its own checks failed or timed out. Re-queued: cancelled or replaced by a later entry, for example behind a failing pull request. Passed: its checks passed.

defaults.noValue: No queue attempt is stored for this pull request. That is no queue history, not no ejections.

value.title: Open the queue comment or run
Open the queue comment or run

panels.title: E2E runs
panels.description: Newest first. One row per suite. A run with test data opens the run page; every other run opens GitHub.

defaults.noValue: No E2E run is stored for this pull request: it ran none, or ran them before the stored history began.

list.name: days
list.label: Window
list.description: Pull requests merged or closed in the last N days.

list.name: pr_author
list.label: Author
list.description: The pull requests of one author, with how many each has in the window. All: everyone.

list.name: wgs
list.label: Working groups to approve
list.query: Any : all,No code owner : 0,1 WG : 1,2 WGs : 2,3+ WGs : 3plus
list.description: The pull requests that needed this many working groups (code-owner teams) to approve, as GitHub reports them. A pull request stored before the lifecycle existed has no count yet and shows under Any only.

list.name: pr_number
list.label: Pull request
list.description: Saved pull requests from the last $days days, of the author and working groups chosen. Type a number to open an open or older pull request.
